outcome: Caller-authored workload dependencies are canonical TypeIDs at the RPC boundary, are proven to exist in the new row's server-resolved owner scope before every enqueue write, and are read through that same owner scope by the scheduler.
securityAssumptions: A workload dependency is private to the dependent row's resolved owner scope. No workload sharing capability exists in the current architecture.

A singular caller therefore may depend only on its own workload rows; a null-owned bulk or system row may depend only on null-owned rows; a targeted bulk-create row may depend only on the resolved target owner's rows.
Admin deployment-wide read authority does not create a durable cross-owner dependency-sharing capability.

Workload rows are retained as an audit log. A user deletion SET NULLs both an owned dependency and its owned dependent; an insert racing the deletion is protected by the dependent row's owner foreign key.

threatModel.attacker: An authenticated user who can call workloads.start and knows or guesses another user's workload id.
inputs: A canonical workload TypeID owned by another user
A canonical TypeID with a non-workload prefix
Malformed nonempty text previously accepted by brandedId
threatModel.before: The router accepted any nonempty dependsOn string. start persisted it without existence or owner validation. resolveDependencyGate later selected dependency status by id alone, so another user's live status controlled the caller's row and malformed or absent text poisoned the queued run.
threatModel.after: The wire rejects noncanonical or wrong-prefix text. start resolves the row owner, uses the central owner-scoped dependency lookup, and collapses absent and foreign ids to workload NOT_FOUND before insert. retry re-proves inherited edges. The scheduler reuses the same scoped lookup, so a directly planted legacy cross-owner edge is treated as absent and fails closed.

afterGraph: findUnavailableWorkloadDependency using id plus owner scope
resolveDependencyGate using the same id plus owner scope
only same-scope status influences the dependent row

attackPathControls: Wrong-prefix and malformed caller values are rejected before WorkloadService.start is invoked.
Missing and foreign ids both throw DomainNotFoundError('workload', id) before a dependent row exists.

A direct persistence fixture bypasses admission with Alice depending on Bob's succeeded row; the scheduler returns no runnable row and durably fails Alice's row. Removing the owner predicate makes this control fail by dispatching Alice's row.
A retry of a legacy Alice row carrying Bob's dependency is refused before a clone exists.

residualRisk: Preexisting cross-owner dependency rows are not migrated. They now fail closed as dependency_failed when scanned. The producer census found no current intentional cross-owner builder, so preserving those edges would require an explicit future sharing capability and stored authority model.

Direct database writers outside the domain could still persist arbitrary JSON. The scheduler's owner-scoped lookup is the defense-in-depth control for that bypass, and retry cannot re-persist such an edge.
This lane did not inspect a live production database for historical cross-owner rows; no live database was opened.
